Attack on Mastriano was an attack on Christianity Out of the gate, U.S. Democrat senators, at the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations hearing held on July 16, 2026, began a coordinated attack upon President Trump’s ambassador nominee to the Slovak Republic, state Sen. Douglas Mastriano. There were four other nominees who received mildly neutral comments and questions, but not Doug Mastriano! Democrat Senator Rosen, in her opening remarks, expressed her serious concerns for his nomination and his credibility. In a red-herring approach to mislead, distract or deflect from his true qualifications, she presented a litany of talking-point accusations, allegedly smearing Mastriano’s reputation. During her period of questioning, Mastriano was berated with criticisms and derogatory remarks, with little to no opportunity for response, only to be repeatedly harassed/interrupted by Rosen and the other Democrat committee members as well. Most seriously was the questioning by Rosen in her attack upon Mastriano’s Christian faith, suggesting that his conservative positions as a Christian would hinder him from service as an ambassador abroad. This was an implied pronouncement against all who claim the name of Christ Jesus as Lord and Savior in their vocation, as does Mastriano, and who stand for the Christian roots of our nation, the same views held by so many of America’s founders. Christians should be concerned about what transpired at this committee hearing. Rosen set up a non sequitur that Mastriano’s Christian views were in conflict with modern America, when asking him if he thought U.S. political leaders should all be Christians. It is comments and questions like Rosen’s that are reckless and dangerous to Christian freedom and patriotic free thinking with an historic appreciation for the foundation of the United States. Douglas Mastriano stands for all that is good in our “one nation under God,” the God in whom we trust! Field commander of the Second Chechen War Khavaji Amaev, who also participated in battles in Syria and Ukraine, was killed in Lviv. For the last 20 years, he had been on the federal wanted list in Russia. On September 30, 1999, Russian troops entered the territory of Chechnya. Thus began and lasted for 10 years (until August 2009) the hostilities in Chechnya and the bordering areas of the North Caucasus, known as the Second Chechen War, the Second Chechen Campaign, or Counter-Terrorist Operations (CTO) in the North Caucasus region. On April 16, 2009, the CTO regime in Chechnya was officially canceled, according to a report from " Caucasian Knot " " Main about the Second Chechen War ". In Lviv, Khavaji Amaev, a native of Chechnya known as "Zumso" - field commander of the Second Chechen War with the rank of colonel of the CRI*, whose squad continued combat operations in the republic until 2012. In recent years, Amaev was a member of the Main Intelligence Directorate (GUR) of Ukraine, TASS reported, citing a source in Russian security forces. 46-year-old Amaev was killed in an apartment; his body with stab wounds to the abdomen was found in the kitchen near the refrigerator. A citizen of Ukraine has been detained on suspicion of murder, and his motive has not yet been established, RTVI reports. A native of the Itum-Kalinsky district of Chechnya and a member of the Zumso teip, Amaev also used the call signs "Abu-Daud", "Abu-Taur", and "Zumso Shishani" at different times. After 2012, Amaev moved to Georgia, then through Turkey to Syria, where he also participated in battles against the forces of Bashar al-Assad's government. In 2014, while in Syria, he recorded a video message to Ramzan Kadyrov, stating that he intended to return to Chechnya and continue the fight. Subsequently, he left Syria by sea and spent two years in a Greek prison for illegal border crossing, claims the Telegram channel Directorate 4. In 2016, Amaev arrived in Poland, where part of his family was already located, and later received refugee status there. Khavaji Amaev participated in hostilities in Ukraine since March 2022. In October of the same year, the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened a case against him for training in terrorist activities, and in June 2026, a case of treason was also initiated against Amaev in Chechnya. Khavaji Amaev had been on the federal wanted list in Russia since 2006. In March 2010, when 21-year-old Anzor Khojaev from the Grozny district was convicted for aiding armed underground groups, security forces stated that he "in particular, assisted the wanted member of the illegal armed formation Khavaji Amaev". In accordance with our government’s decision, the infrastructure used by the Border Guard is being strengthened,” Kosiniak-Kamysz wrote on X following the two weekend strikes, one of which hit a train as a group of former Western officials were traveling in the area. “Soldiers of the 18th Engineer Regiment are ‌already carrying out tasks, thanks to which the checkpoints and infrastructure near the Polish-Ukrainian border will ⁠be reinforced.” The Russian Ministry of Defense on Tuesday confirmed two strikes near the Polish border, claiming the train had been transporting military cargo. Earlier Tuesday, military officials in Lithuania, another NATO member, said a drone had been shot down in the country’s airspace for the first time. The drone was equipped with an explosive device, which was neutralized by bomb disposal experts, according to the Lithuanian Ministry of Defense. An investigation is ongoing to determine the origin of the drone, the ministry told CNN. On Wednesday, Lithuania’s president said the drone was of a type used by Russia and had likely been targeting Ukraine. “It was most likely not a conscious action against Lithuania. It (the drone) was probably targeted towards Ukraine but affected by Ukrainian electronic warfare and deviated off course,” President Gitanas Nauseda told reporters, according to Reuters. Italy’s defense minister, Guido Crosetto, said an Italian NATO fighter jet shot down the drone, adding that it “most probably came from Russia.” The Italian Defense Ministry said in a statement that it was the second incident involving the country’s fighter jets in the space of a month. “It is also because of incidents like this that the presence of our military on the Eastern Flank is crucial for ensuring communitarian security,” Crosetto said. Also on Tuesday, the Danish Armed Forces said a Danish military helicopter was targeted by a Russian warship, which fired two emergency flares while the helicopter was taking routine photographs of the vessel in international waters on Monday. Following the incident, Ukrainian Minister of Foreign Affairs Andrii Sybiha expressed support for Denmark “in the wake of Russia’s provocative and unacceptable action.” “Moscow continues its attempts to destabilize Europe, not just Denmark,” he added in a post on X, calling for joint and decisive action to protect Europe from Russian threats. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said Monday that strikes close to NATO territory reflected Russian President Vladimir Putin’s “desperation” and his desire “to sow fear and terror.” Rutte has pledged to bolster the 32-nation alliance’s defenses along its border with Russia and its close ally Belarus. Meanwhile, the United States appears to be working to stop Ukraine and Russia from hitting each other’s energy targets amid concerns over the global spike in fuel prices . US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the countries agreed to halt energy-related attacks, but both his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky and the Kremlin later described it as a proposal rather than a firm agreement . Ukraine has been hammering Russian fuel infrastructure for months, severely reducing Moscow’s refining capacity and triggering widespread supply shortages. In response, Russia has banned the foreign sale of its diesel. “There is now a strong US proposal for a mutual halt to strikes on critical infrastructure,” Zelensky said on Monday night. “If this can become the first de-escalatory step – a step toward ending Russian strikes on our critical infrastructure and our strikes in response – then Ukraine is ready to support de-escalation.” CNN’s Lauren Kent and Stefano Pozzebon contributed to this report The-CNN-Wire ™ & © 2026 Cable News Network, Inc., a Warner Bros.
